title: B Cells in Disguise: Myeloma-Defining Events, Waldenström MYD88 and the Hodgkin Cell
summary: Apply the IMWG MGUS, smoldering and myeloma criteria (CRAB and biomarker events, progression rates), recognise Waldenström macroglobulinemia and the limits of MYD88 L265P, and read the CD30/CD15/CD45 phenotype of classic Hodgkin lymphoma.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 34 Hit 11 (myeloma CRAB, MGUS and smoldering progression), Hit 12 (Reed-Sternberg phenotype, nodular sclerosis) and Hit 13 (Waldenström macroglobulinemia, MYD88 L265P), checked against Rajkumar 2024 (IMWG criteria; read via a page-fetch tool), Lakshman 2018, Bibas 2024, Satou 2022, Momotow 2021 and Gajzer & Fromm 2025. Hit 11 defines myeloma by CRAB alone; since 2014 the IMWG also counts three biomarkers (plasma cells ≥60%, FLC ratio ≥100, >1 MRI focal lesion). Hit 11 smoldering progression (“10%/year for 5 years”) depends on the definition era and risk group. Hit 13 implies MYD88 L265P identifies WM; it is in ~90–95% of WM but also in many IgM MGUS and in ABC-type DLBCL. Hit 12 gives CD15+ as fixed; it is variable (most cases). Not taught (pending): the “young women” sex predominance of nodular sclerosis and the Reed-Sternberg “owl eye” morphology, neither found in the sources read.

objectives: Classify a plasma cell disorder as MGUS, smoldering myeloma or multiple myeloma using M-protein, marrow plasma cells and myeloma-defining events.
List the CRAB cut-offs and the three biomarker myeloma-defining events, and state approximate MGUS and smoldering progression rates.
Recognise Waldenström macroglobulinemia and explain why MYD88 L265P supports but does not prove it.
Identify the Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cell phenotype and contrast it with nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

scenes.title: Three B-cell disguises
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three patients. (1) A 66-year-old with calcium 12.1 mg/dL, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, Hb 9.1 g/dL, lytic lesions on CT, an IgG kappa M-protein and 35% clonal marrow plasma cells. (2) A 70-year-old with an IgM kappa M-protein of 4.2 g/dL, blurred vision and nosebleeds; the marrow shows lymphoplasmacytic cells. (3) A 24-year-old with a mediastinal mass; the node shows scattered large CD30+ CD15+ CD45− cells in an inflammatory background. Question token: “Which B-cell neoplasm hides in each?”

cues.text: Three patients. A sixty-six-year-old with high calcium, a creatinine of two point four, a haemoglobin of nine, lytic bone lesions, an IgG kappa M-protein and thirty-five percent clonal marrow plasma cells.
A seventy-year-old with an IgM kappa M-protein of four point two grams per decilitre, blurred vision and nosebleeds.
And a twenty-four-year-old with a mediastinal mass and rare large CD30-positive, CD15-positive, CD45-negative cells in an inflamed node. Which B-cell neoplasm hides in each?

props.label: Which B-cell neoplasm hides in each?

scenes.title: The plasma cell spectrum
scenes.altText: Three cards (IMWG criteria as given in Rajkumar 2024). MGUS (non-IgM): serum M-protein <3 g/dL, clonal marrow plasma cells <10%, no CRAB damage; progresses at about 1% per year. Smoldering myeloma: serum IgG/IgA M-protein ≥3 g/dL or urine M-protein ≥500 mg/24 h, and/or clonal marrow plasma cells 10–60%, with no myeloma-defining event or amyloidosis. Multiple myeloma: clonal marrow plasma cells ≥10% or a biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, plus at least one myeloma-defining event. Token: clone size sets MGUS vs smoldering; a myeloma-defining event makes it myeloma.

cues.text: Start with the plasma cell spectrum. MGUS means a non-IgM M-protein below three grams per decilitre, fewer than ten percent clonal marrow plasma cells, and no CRAB organ damage. It progresses at about one percent per year.

Smoldering myeloma means an M-protein of three grams per decilitre or more, or urine M-protein of five hundred milligrams a day or more, and or ten to sixty percent clonal marrow plasma cells, with no myeloma-defining event.
Multiple myeloma needs ten percent or more clonal marrow plasma cells, or a biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, plus at least one myeloma-defining event.
So the size of the clone separates MGUS from smoldering myeloma, but it is the myeloma-defining event that turns a smoldering clone into myeloma.

props.label: Clone size grades · an event diagnoses

scenes.title: CRAB, SLiM and the progression clock
scenes.altText: CRAB card (IMWG cut-offs, Rajkumar 2024): hyperCalcaemia (>1 mg/dL above ULN or >11 mg/dL); Renal (creatinine clearance <40 mL/min or creatinine >2 mg/dL); Anaemia (Hb >2 g/dL below LLN or <10 g/dL); Bone (≥1 osteolytic lesion on radiography, CT or PET-CT). Biomarker card (added 2014): clonal marrow plasma cells ≥60%; involved:uninvolved serum free light chain ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L; >1 focal MRI lesion ≥5 mm — in smoldering myeloma these carried about an 80% risk of progression at 2 years (Lakshman 2018). Progression card: MGUS ~1%/year; smoldering myeloma about 10%/year for 5 years then lower (Rajkumar 2024); in a 2014-criteria cohort, 18% in year 1, ~10%/year for the next 3 years, ~4%/year after (Lakshman 2018). Risk token: marrow plasma cells >20%, M-protein >2 g/dL, FLC ratio >20.

cues.text: Myeloma-defining events start with CRAB. Calcium more than one milligram per decilitre above the upper limit, or above eleven. Creatinine clearance below forty, or creatinine above two. Haemoglobin two grams below the lower limit, or below ten. And one or more lytic bone lesions on X-ray, CT or PET-CT.

Since 2014, three biomarkers also count, even without CRAB: sixty percent or more clonal plasma cells, a free light chain ratio of one hundred or more with the involved chain at least one hundred milligrams per litre, or more than one focal lesion on MRI. In smoldering myeloma these carried about an eighty percent risk of progression within two years.

Then the clock. MGUS progresses at about one percent per year. Smoldering myeloma runs about ten percent per year for the first five years, then slower. In one cohort defined by the 2014 criteria, eighteen percent progressed in the first year, about ten percent per year for the next three, then about four.
Smoldering risk is not one number. Marrow plasma cells above twenty percent, M-protein above two grams per decilitre and a light chain ratio above twenty each shortened the time to progression.

props.title: CRAB events
lines: C: Ca > 1 above ULN or > 11 mg/dL
A: Hb 2 below LLN or < 10 g/dL

scenes.title: IgM lymphoma and the Hodgkin cell
scenes.altText: Waldenström card: IgM M-protein of any size plus lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma in the marrow; MYD88 L265P in about 90–95% (allele-specific PCR); CXCR4 mutations in 30–40%, linked to hyperviscosity and BTK-inhibitor resistance; retinal exam if IgM >3 g/dL; asymptomatic WM is observed, not treated. Not-exclusive card: MYD88 mutations in about 50–90% of IgM MGUS and in ABC-type DLBCL; absence does not rule out LPL; IgM myeloma has plasmacytic marrow infiltration, lytic lesions, renal insufficiency, t(11;14) and no MYD88 mutation. Hodgkin card (classic HL): HRS cells universally CD30+, variably CD15+ (89% by flow cytometry), CD45−, CD20 negative or weak, weak PAX5, in a reactive inflammatory background. Hook answers: (1) myeloma (CRAB); (2) Waldenström pattern, check MYD88 and hyperviscosity; (3) classic Hodgkin, nodular sclerosis pattern (70–80% of classic HL in Western countries, mainly adolescents, frequent mediastinal mass).

cues.text: An IgM M-protein of any size with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma in the marrow defines Waldenström macroglobulinemia. MYD88 L265P is found in about ninety to ninety-five percent. CXCR4 mutations, in thirty to forty percent, go with hyperviscosity and BTK-inhibitor resistance.

But MYD88 is not exclusive: about half to ninety percent of IgM MGUS carry it, so does activated B-cell diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and its absence does not rule out the disease. IgM myeloma has plasma cells, lytic lesions and t(11;14), and lacks the MYD88 mutation.

In classic Hodgkin lymphoma, the Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells are few, set in an inflammatory crowd. They are universally CD30 positive, CD15 positive in most cases, and CD45 negative, with weak or absent CD20 and weak PAX5.

Back to the hook. Patient one has myeloma, with every CRAB event. Patient two fits Waldenström with hyperviscosity, so check MYD88 and examine the retina. Patient three fits classic Hodgkin, likely nodular sclerosis: seventy to eighty percent of classic cases in Western countries, mainly affecting adolescents, often with a mediastinal mass.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “No CRAB means not myeloma” (✓ plasma cells ≥60%, FLC ratio ≥100 or >1 MRI focal lesion are myeloma-defining events too); “MYD88 L265P proves Waldenström” (✓ it is also common in IgM MGUS and found in ABC-type DLBCL; a negative result does not exclude LPL); “Every Hodgkin cell is CD30+ CD15+” (✓ CD15 is variable in classic HL; nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL has CD20+ LP cells that lack CD30, and CD15 is rare).

cues.text: Trap one: no CRAB means no myeloma. No: sixty percent or more plasma cells, a light chain ratio of one hundred or more, or more than one MRI focal lesion are myeloma-defining events too.
Trap two: MYD88 L265P proves Waldenström. No: it is common in IgM MGUS and found in other lymphomas, and a negative result does not exclude the disease.
Trap three: every Hodgkin cell is CD30 and CD15 positive. No: CD15 is variable, and in nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma the LP cells are CD20 positive and lack CD30.

scenes.title: The crab, the slim crab and the IgM giant
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The CRAB walks in with four claws — Calcium, Renal, Anaemia, Bone. Its SLiM cousin needs no claws: Sixty percent, Light-chain ratio one hundred, MRI lesions. The IgM giant carries a MYD88 badge, but so do some of its harmless relatives. The Hodgkin cell always wears 30, usually 15, never 45.” Tokens: CRAB = organ damage · SLiM = biomarkers · IgM + LPL = WM · 30+ 15± 45− = HRS. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the CRAB walks in with four claws: calcium, renal, anaemia, bone. Its slim cousin needs no claws: sixty percent, light chain ratio one hundred, MRI lesions. The IgM giant carries a MYD88 badge, and the Hodgkin cell always wears thirty, usually fifteen, never forty-five.

Where it breaks: the light chain ratio also needs an involved chain of at least one hundred milligrams per litre; MYD88 is shared with IgM MGUS and other lymphomas; and the lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin cell usually does not wear thirty.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Myeloma = plasma cells ≥10% + CRAB or SLiM event”, “WM = IgM + LPL (MYD88 supports) · HRS = CD30+ CD45− CD15±”.

cues.text: Myeloma needs clonal plasma cells plus a CRAB or biomarker event, Waldenström needs an IgM protein with lymphoplasmacytic marrow infiltration that MYD88 supports but does not prove, and classic Hodgkin cells are CD30-positive and CD45-negative with variable CD15.

props.label: Myeloma = plasma cells ≥ 10% + CRAB or SLiM event
WM = IgM + LPL (MYD88 supports) · HRS = CD30+ CD45− CD15±

explanation.what: Plain language: these are B-cell cancers that do not look like ordinary B cells. Myeloma is a cancer of antibody-making plasma cells, Waldenström macroglobulinemia is a slow lymphoma that makes large IgM antibodies, and Hodgkin lymphoma has a few large abnormal cells hidden among many normal inflammatory cells. Scientific terms: monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), smoldering multiple myeloma, myeloma-defining events (CRAB and biomarkers), serum free light chain ratio, lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL), MYD88 L265P, CXCR4, Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells, CD30, CD15, CD45, nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL).
explanation.why: Much of the harm in myeloma comes from organ damage, so the 2014 IMWG revision reclassified ultra-high-risk smoldering patients, those with a biomarker carrying about an 80% risk of progression at 2 years, as myeloma needing therapy. In WM, IgM-related complications such as hyperviscosity can cause symptoms. HRS cells show reduced B-cell markers (CD20 weak or absent), lack CD45 and express CD30.
explanation.measure: Serum protein electrophoresis/immunofixation and free light chains; marrow plasma cell percentage; calcium, creatinine or creatinine clearance, haemoglobin; skeletal CT/PET-CT and MRI. WM: IgM quantitation, marrow biopsy, MYD88 L265P (allele-specific PCR), retinal exam if IgM >3 g/dL. Hodgkin: tissue immunohistochemistry or flow cytometry for CD30, CD15, CD45, CD20, PAX5.
explanation.differs: MGUS (M-protein <3 g/dL, plasma cells <10%, no CRAB) vs smoldering (≥3 g/dL and/or 10–60%, no event) vs myeloma (≥10% or plasmacytoma plus an event); WM (IgM, lymphoplasmacytic, MYD88 usually mutated) vs IgM myeloma (plasma cells, lytic lesions, t(11;14), MYD88 wild-type); classic HL (CD30+, CD15 usually +, CD45−) vs NLPHL (CD20+, CD30−, CD15 rare).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: classify a plasma cell disorder from numbers, recognise a biomarker-only myeloma, name the mutation associated with WM, or pick classic Hodgkin from a CD30+/CD15+/CD45− phenotype.

mnemonic.text: The CRAB walks in with four claws — Calcium, Renal, Anaemia, Bone. Its SLiM cousin needs no claws: Sixty percent, Light-chain ratio one hundred, MRI lesions. The IgM giant carries a MYD88 badge, and the Hodgkin cell always wears 30, usually 15, never 45.
mnemonic.explanation: Groups the two kinds of myeloma-defining events, ties IgM and MYD88 to Waldenström, and encodes the HRS phenotype CD30+, CD15 usually +, CD45−.
mnemonic.limitation: The free light chain criterion also needs an involved light chain of at least 100 mg/L; MYD88 L265P is shared with IgM MGUS and other lymphomas and is absent in some WM; nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin cells usually lack CD30 (at most minimal by flow cytometry).

analogyLimitations: Cards are schematic; no micrographs, electrophoresis strips or flow plots.
The crab and giant images are memory devices, not biology.
takeaway: Myeloma needs clonal plasma cells plus a CRAB or biomarker event, Waldenström needs an IgM protein with lymphoplasmacytic marrow infiltration that MYD88 supports but does not prove, and classic Hodgkin cells are CD30-positive and CD45-negative with variable CD15.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old followed for smoldering myeloma has normal calcium, creatinine and haemoglobin and no lytic lesions, but a new marrow biopsy shows 65% clonal plasma cells. How should this now be classified under IMWG criteria?

options.rationale: Correct. Clonal marrow plasma cells of 60% or more is a biomarker myeloma-defining event, so myeloma is diagnosed even without CRAB features.

options.text: Smoldering myeloma, because there are no CRAB features
options.rationale: Incorrect. Smoldering myeloma is limited to 10–60% plasma cells with no myeloma-defining event; since 2014, 60% or more counts as an event.
Incorrect. MGUS requires fewer than 10% clonal marrow plasma cells.
Incorrect. Waldenström needs an IgM M-protein with lymphoplasmacytic (not purely plasma cell) marrow infiltration.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old has an IgM kappa M-protein of 4.2 g/dL, blurred vision and lymphoplasmacytic cells in the marrow, without lytic bone lesions. Which statement about MYD88 L265P testing is accurate?

options.text: It is found in about 90–95% of Waldenström cases, supports the diagnosis, but is also common in IgM MGUS
options.rationale: Correct. MYD88 L265P is detected in about 90–95% of WM by allele-specific PCR, but about 50–90% of IgM MGUS also carry MYD88 mutations, so it supports rather than proves WM.

options.text: A negative result excludes Waldenström macroglobulinemia
options.rationale: Incorrect. Lack of a MYD88 mutation does not rule out lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.

options.text: It is the hallmark mutation of IgM myeloma
options.rationale: Incorrect. IgM myeloma lacks MYD88 mutations; t(11;14) and lytic lesions point to it.

options.text: It is only found in Waldenström macroglobulinemia
options.rationale: Incorrect. MYD88 mutations also occur in IgM MGUS and in activated B-cell type diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

questions.stem: A lymph node from a young adult with a mediastinal mass contains rare large cells that are CD30+, CD15+, CD45− and CD20 weak, surrounded by many reactive lymphocytes, histiocytes and eosinophils. Which diagnosis fits best?

options.rationale: Correct. HRS cells are CD30+, usually CD15+, CD45− with weak or absent CD20, in an inflammatory background; nodular sclerosis is the most common subtype and often has a mediastinal mass.
Incorrect. Its LP cells are CD20+ with strong B-cell transcription factors and lack CD30; CD15 is rarely expressed.
Incorrect. Follicular lymphoma cells are CD45+, CD20+ and CD10+ with light-chain restriction, not CD30+/CD15+ CD45− cells.
Incorrect. Myeloma is a clonal plasma cell disorder of the marrow, not CD30+/CD15+ large cells in a node.

claims.text: Non-IgM MGUS: M-protein <3 g/dL, clonal plasma cells <10%, no CRAB; progresses ~1%/year.
Smoldering myeloma: M-protein ≥3 g/dL or urine ≥500 mg/24 h and/or plasma cells 10–60%, no myeloma-defining event.
Myeloma: plasma cells ≥10% or plasmacytoma plus ≥1 myeloma-defining event; CRAB cut-offs.
Biomarker events since 2014: plasma cells ≥60%, FLC ratio ≥100 with involved ≥100 mg/L, >1 MRI focal lesion ≥5 mm; ~80% 2-year progression risk in smoldering myeloma.

Smoldering progression ~10%/year for the first 5 years then lower; 2014-criteria cohort 18% year 1, ~10%/year next 3 years, ~4%/year after; risk factors >20% plasma cells, M-protein >2 g/dL, FLC ratio >20.
WM: IgM of any size plus marrow LPL; MYD88 L265P ~90–95%; CXCR4 30–40% with hyperviscosity and BTK-inhibitor resistance; retinal exam if IgM >3 g/dL; asymptomatic WM observed.
MYD88 mutations in ~50–90% of IgM MGUS and in ABC-DLBCL; absence does not exclude LPL; IgM myeloma has plasma cells, lytic lesions, renal insufficiency, t(11;14), no MYD88 mutation.
HRS cells universally CD30+, CD15+ in most (89% by flow), CD45−, CD20 negative or weak, weak PAX5, in an inflammatory background.
Nodular sclerosis: 70–80% of classic HL in Western countries, mainly adolescents, frequent mediastinal mass.
NLPHL LP cells CD20+, lack CD30, CD15 rare.
Reviewer Hit 12: nodular sclerosis is the “young women” subtype — sex predominance not found in the sources read; not taught.
Reviewer Memory Hook: Reed-Sternberg “owl eye” bilobed nuclei with huge nucleoli — morphology not checked against an open source; not taught.
“The crab, the slim crab and the IgM giant.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Hit 11 defines myeloma as CRAB plus clonal marrow plasma cells. Since the 2014 IMWG revision, clonal plasma cells ≥60%, an involved:uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 (involved FLC ≥100 mg/L) or >1 MRI focal lesion ≥5 mm are also myeloma-defining events (Rajkumar 2024; Lakshman 2018). The lesson teaches CRAB and the biomarkers (register flag rv-ch34-myeloma-biomarker-events).

Hit 11 and the Number Vault give smoldering progression as 10%/year for 5 years, then 3%, then 1%, which matches the smoldering section of Rajkumar 2024 (its introduction gives 1.5% for the late rate). These figures are not fixed: in a cohort defined by the 2014 criteria (Lakshman 2018) it was 18% in year 1, ~10%/year for 3 years and ~4%/year after, with large differences by risk group (5%/year low risk vs 24%/year high risk in the first 2 years). The lesson teaches the approximate figure and its dependence on definition and risk (register flag rv-ch34-smm-progression-rates).

Hit 13 pairs WM with MYD88 L265P as if diagnostic. Bibas 2024 gives MYD88 L265P in about 90–95% of WM by AS-PCR but also MYD88 mutations in about 50–90% of IgM MGUS and in ABC-type DLBCL, and states that lack of the mutation does not rule out LPL. The lesson teaches MYD88 as supportive (register flag rv-ch34-myd88-supports-not-proves).

Hit 12 gives Reed-Sternberg cells as CD15+ without qualification and calls nodular sclerosis the young-women subtype. Satou 2022 describes HRS cells as universally CD30+ but variably CD15+ (89% by flow cytometry in Gajzer 2025), and nodular sclerosis as mainly affecting adolescents with frequent mediastinal mass; no sex predominance was found in the sources read (register flag rv-ch34-hrs-cd15-variable).

morphology.note: No micrographs, electrophoresis strips or real flow plots; criteria and phenotypes shown as cards.

verification.notes: 10 claims checked against Rajkumar 2024 (read via a page-fetch tool), Lakshman 2018, Bibas 2024, Satou 2022, Momotow 2021 and Gajzer & Fromm 2025 (the last five read as Europe PMC full text); 2 pending (nodular sclerosis sex predominance; Reed-Sternberg owl-eye morphology), neither taught. No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
